getting-started.title: Start here: your first shoot
getting-started.body:
Open a card or folder, choose keepers, add details, and import verified copies. Save the setup for next time.

You’ll need an Apple silicon Mac with macOS 15 or later, a card reader or photo folder, and a destination with enough space. Lightroom Classic is optional. Transfer time depends on your card, drive, and files.

On first launch, Welcome to Ingest offers an optional overview of the Command Palette, Workspaces, review, Photo Groups, Metadata Assist, and Decks. Jump to any topic, then choose whether to build your first workspace at Get Started. Reopen it through Help → Welcome to Ingest or the Command Palette. The steps below walk through your first import.

1. Insert2. Review3. Metadata4. Copy5. Set up

  1. Plug in your SD card.

    With Ingest running, insert your camera card. A newly detected card opens in Browse when Settings → Transfers → Open a card when it is inserted is enabled. It is on by default. If the card was connected before launch, choose it from Cards & drives.

    Choose a source in the left sidebar, or press ⌘O to open a photo folder. Browse is where you review photos. Import… in the toolbar opens Import Settings; opening it does not start a copy.

    Find it with ⌘K: type “Open Folder” or “Find Folder”.

  2. Review your keepers.

    Use the arrow keys to move through the shoot. Press T to tag a keeper; press it again to untag. Space opens a larger Preview and returns to your previous view.

    Choose Show: Tagged above the grid to revisit your keepers. When you open Import…, its scope starts at Selected if photos are selected, otherwise All. Choose Tagged explicitly to copy your tagged photos. Browse filters and import scope are separate. Check the count in Import Settings; an empty scope stays empty.

    Select two photos and press C to compare. In Preview, Z toggles Fit / 100%. Find Grid Loupe, Focus Peaking, and Detail Overlay in the View menu. Stack review keeps bursts and exposure brackets together.

    These are the default keys. Your customized shortcuts appear in the app walkthrough. See the keyboard reference or open Settings → Shortcuts.

    Find it with ⌘K: type “Tag” or “Show Tagged Only”.

  3. Add shoot details with Metadata Assist.

    Open Import…, then choose Edit Shoot Details beside Shoot details. Metadata Assist stages shared details for this import. Choose Keywords, Caption, IPTC Place, or GPS Location, or type ; to find a field. Tab completes remembered values.

    Check Review changes. Use Edit Individual Fields… for detailed IPTC fields, or Find or use saved place… for a map location. Choose Use for Import to return the reviewed draft to Import Settings. Details go to verified copies; card originals stay unchanged.

    For existing writable files, select photos in Browse and press ⌘’. Here, Apply writes the reviewed metadata to those files or their RAW sidecars. Check the photo scope before applying. Import shoot details and edits to existing files are separate uses of the same editor.

    Metadata Assist guide →

  4. Copy, back up, and hand off to Lightroom.

    In Import Settings, choose Save to under Destination. Add a backup destination on another physical drive if you want a second verified copy. Review Subfolders and Filenames, then inspect the output paths on the right.

    Use a separate physical drive for Photo Backup. Ingest’s second verified copy is one part of a backup workflow: arrange off-site protection and editor/catalog backups separately. A Lightroom catalog backup does not back up your original photographs. See 3-2-1 backup guidance.

    Optionally expand After Import, add Open in Lightroom Classic, and choose Photos for this action. For example, import All while opening only Tagged copies in Classic. Check the import count, action count, and destinations, then click Import. After copying, metadata processing, and verification succeed, Classic receives the matching files for you to review and confirm its import.

    Classic must be installed. If its action is missing or the app lives elsewhere, configure it in Settings → Automation. You can also import the destination folder from Classic yourself. Set up the Lightroom handoff →

    For your first import, keep Leave the card alone. Import Progress opens automatically; Continue Browsing lets you keep working. Wait for Import Complete and the verification result before ejecting. Understand copy and verification results →

  5. Save the setup for next time.

    Open Settings → Workspaces → New Workspace… and choose Use Workspace Builder or Set Up Manually. Start from scratch or preview Events, Headshots, or Real Estate, then choose its Use button.

    Choose your folders and filenames. Insert questions where you need answers, then check the preview of what you will be asked at import. Organize stores separate defaults for existing photos; Photo Groups are configured in Import Settings. Review and save. Use Workspace applies your setup without starting an import.

    Project folders that separate source photographs from outputs are an approach also used by Capture One Sessions. The homepage examples (Wedding, Landscapes, Personal, Headshots, Events) are ideas for your own workspaces. The builder’s built-in starters are Build from scratch, Events, Headshots, and Real Estate.

    • Wedding: capture-order Grid, burst grouping, client filenames, and a backup.
    • Landscapes: Split view, exposure-bracket stacks, and original camera filenames.
    • Personal: simple folders, Preview, and optional Apple Photos.
    • Headshots: client filenames, paired RAW + JPEG, and video excluded from import.
    • Events: event filenames and a workspace TSV file of caption codes.

    Set up workspaces →   Metadata templates →   Automation →

    Apple Photos has a global switch in Settings → General and a switch for each workspace. Keep it on for Personal and off for Headshots; the global switch must also be on. Learn about Apple Photos →

    One shortcut to keep: ⌘K. In the app, type “Workspace” to find your saved setups, “walkthrough” to revisit these steps, or the name of whatever you want to do next. On this site, ⌘K searches pages and sections the same way.

Try it at your own pace.

Full guide →Keyboard reference →

templates.title: Names and metadata that fit the job.
templates.body:
Keep original filenames, or type names and insert readable variables in Import File Names or Organize. Advanced pattern exposes the same pattern as text. This reference explains the {…} tokens used in names and folders, and ; for finding fields in Metadata Assist.

Try {…}

Curly braces fill rename and folder variables. Edit the template and watch the filename. Semicolon finds metadata fields in Metadata Assist — that habit is shown in the app, not here.

How a template works Every token The sequence number Examples Subfolders When names collide Quick entry Snippets

How a template works

Curly braces rename. Anything in braces is replaced; anything else is kept as you typed it. So {yyyy}{mm}{dd}-{seqn} becomes 20260912-0001, and Wedding-{seq} becomes Wedding-1. Semicolon is a different habit — it finds metadata fields in Metadata Assist, not tokens in a name.

Some tokens take an argument after a colon. {seqn:4} sets the width of the number, {date:MMMM d, yyyy} sets a date format. To write a real brace, double it: {{ and }}.

Templates are used in four places: renaming during ingest, renaming in place with ⌘R, naming the subfolder that ingest creates, and filling in captions and titles in a metadata preset. Settings → Naming keeps your saved templates and shows a live example as you type.

A template also decides letter case, what spaces turn into, and the case of the extension. The workspace naming editor preserves the spaces and separators you type. Review the resolved preview and any saved recipe’s case and spacing choices.

A token that has no value disappears, and takes the separator next to it with it, so a missing address does not leave a stray hyphen at the front of every name.

Every token

Insert Variable lists readable choices in workspace naming editors. Ask when importing inserts an answer such as Client; New Question… adds your own. Only answers used by names or metadata are requested at import. What do the variables mean? explains each variable, and Photo Number options… sets the starting number and digit width. Type { to search variables directly. Advanced pattern and other template editors also support the tokens below.

Numbers

TokenValue
{seqn}The saved counter: per project during ingest, otherwise shared across jobs. See below.
{seq}A counter for this job only, starting at whatever you put in the start field.
{frame}The number the camera gave the file. DSC01206 gives 01206.
{stack}Which bracket set this photograph belongs to. Empty for photographs that are not in one.
{stackframe}Which frame within that set.

All five take a width: {seqn:4} gives 0001. Widths from 1 to 12.

Legacy Social Export naming

The built-in Social Export editor was removed in Ingest 0.9.6. Use Send to Decks… to compose and export in Decks. Existing exported filenames are unchanged. Ordinary Ingest filename templates remain available.

Photo Groups and Organize

{group} is the group name, {groupnumber} its number (two digits by default), and {groupseq} the sequence within it (three digits by default). Explicit widths such as {groupseq:4} are supported. Named Photo Groups can use these during import without creating extra folders: {groupnumber:2} {group} {groupseq:4} can produce 01 Cocktail Hour 0001.jpg.

Within a saved shoot, group numbering continues across cards. Allocations remain reserved for retries; changing a group name or order does not rename existing files. A new shoot starts fresh. If the chosen filename or folder needs a group, assign remaining photos before importing.

{shoot} uses the shoot name. {input:key} uses a question’s internal identifier; the visual editor inserts it for you as Answer: Client or your question’s label. Missing required answers block import with an explanation.

The file itself

TokenValue
{base}The original name without its extension. Takes upper or lower.
{filename}The same thing, under its other name.
{ext}The original extension.
{folder}The name of the folder the photograph came from.
{dest}The name of the folder it is going to.

Import, task, and capture dates

TokenValue
{importdate:yyyy-MM-dd}Import Date. Available for import names and folders; unavailable in Organize.
{today:yyyy-MM-dd}Today’s Date for the import or Organize task.
{date:yyyy-MM-dd}The capture date in any format you like. {date:MMM d} gives Sep 12.
{yyyy} {yy}Year, four digits or two.
{mm} {dd}Month and day.
{hh} {mn} {ss}Hour, minute, second.

Capture Date and the year/month/day/time pieces read the file’s capture time, falling back to its modification date. For a containing folder, Capture Date uses the earliest photo date in the selection. Import Date and Today’s Date use the task’s date instead; Import Date can keep photographs taken across several days together.

The camera

These work in filenames. They are left out of the subfolder menu because a whole folder of photographs rarely shares one exposure.

TokenValue
{model}Camera model, such as ILCE-7RM5. Job folder templates use a source photo’s camera model; Settings labels its sample camera when no source model is available.
{lens}Lens model.
{iso}ISO.
{shutter}Shutter speed, made safe for a filename: 1/500 becomes 1-500.
{aperture}f8. With {aperture:raw}, just 8.
{fl}16mm. With {fl:raw}, just 16.
{ev}Exposure compensation: 0, +0.7, -1.3.

Where it was taken

TokenValue
{address}The job address, set in Ingest or with ⌘L, formatted for filenames using the chosen Spaces setting. The same address can fill a metadata template’s Property address prompt.
{street}The same value.
{city} {state} {zip}The rest of the address.

The sequence number

During ingest, {seqn} uses the current project’s saved counter. A new project starts at 0001, and another card for that project continues where the first stopped. Outside a project, it uses the shared counter across jobs. Start at shows the next number and accepts an override. Different projects can use the same numbers.

The width comes from the zeros you type. 0001 in the start field gives four digits, so 7078 comes out as 7078 and 42 comes out as 0042. Leading zeros are what keep files in order when something sorts them as text.

Planning a job does not move the counter. Review the proposed names before copying. The counter is recorded as files are published, so an interrupted job can already have used numbers for its completed copies.

Settings → Naming shows the next sequence number and lets you change it. Review the starting number for the current project or job. Resetting or overriding a counter can reuse earlier numbers; the collision check still protects files already at the destination.

{seq} is the other counter: it starts wherever you say, for this job only, and it is the right choice when a client wants photographs numbered from one.

Examples

TemplateResult
{seqn}7078.arw
{yyyy}{mm}{dd}-{base}20260912-DSC01206.jpg
{address}-{seqn}1428-Maple-St-7078.arw
{date:yyyy-MM-dd}-{city}-{seq:3}2026-09-12-Seaside-001.jpg
{base}-{stack}-{stackframe}DSC01210-1-1.jpg, for the first frame of the first bracket set
{model}-{fl}-{seqn}ILCE-7RM5-16mm-7078.arw

A combined RAW and JPEG / HEIF pair gets the same base name with the appropriate extensions, so 20260912-DSC01206.arw and 20260912-DSC01206.jpg stay together wherever they go.

Subfolders

Your workspace’s import settings can put each job in its own folder, named by the same kind of template. {date:yyyy-MM-dd} gives 2026-09-12, and {address} gives a folder per listing.

Subfolder templates cannot use the per file tokens, because a folder cannot have a different name for each photograph inside it. {seqn}, {seq}, {frame}, {base}, {ext}, {stack}, and {stackframe} are refused with an explanation rather than silently ignored.

When names collide

Ingest never overwrites a file and never quietly adds a suffix to make room. If two photographs would get the same name, or a name already exists at the destination, it says so before it starts and will not begin until you fix it.

The messages are specific: how many photographs would share a name, which name already exists, or that only the letter case differs. The hint is always the same, because the answer usually is: add {seqn} or {seq} so every name is unique.

Renaming in place has one extra case. If a name would not actually change, Ingest tells you rather than doing nothing and looking broken.

Metadata Assist and Quick Entry

Semicolon finds fields. ⌘’ opens Metadata Assist with explicit review before applying. Type ; to see your field options, pick one, then Tab to take it and fill or search. Read the complete guide.

Values you stage here (client, event, location, shoot date) can feed rename templates through curly-brace tokens such as {client}, {event}, {location}, and {shootdate}. Missing required shoot values block planning. These do not change camera capture timestamps.

Caption-code files are configured per workspace: UTF-8 TSV, a code followed by tab-separated replacements, normally invoked with =. Later files take precedence. Choose alternatives with #n; unknown or cyclic codes must be resolved before importing.

Press Q for the earlier Quick Entry syntax. Enter the line, review the proposed fields, then apply to the selection. The order does not matter and most of it is optional.

You typeIt means
coast sunriseTwo keywords. Bare words are keywords.
front yard, kitchenWith a comma anywhere in the line, each comma separated run is one keyword. So this is two keywords, not three.
#familyA keyword, even when the word would otherwise mean something else.
3* *** 3 starsThree stars. 0* clears the rating.
red r 🔴A color label. Also yellow, green, blue, purple, and their first letters.
"First light at the pier"The caption. Curly quotes work too, and a quote you never close runs to the end of the line.
@Ecola State ParkPropose a descriptive place name, through the next comma or end of the line. Use Find place to explicitly choose a GPS map pin.
/listingApply the metadata preset with that name.
;addrExpand a snippet. See below.
t tag untagApply or remove a tag. Stars, colors, and keywords are independent.

The one rule worth knowing: a word like red counts as a command only when its whole comma separated segment is commands. So red door, kitchen gives you two keywords, and kitchen, red gives you a keyword and a color. That is what lets you write ordinary English without escaping anything.

The same line works from a link, which is how an external script or a Stream Deck button can mark a photograph. See the URL scheme.

Snippets

A snippet is a short name that expands into longer text. Type ;addr in quick entry, a caption, or the keyword field, and it becomes whatever you defined, tokens and all.

The shipped one is ;addr, which expands to {address}, {city} {state}. Settings → Metadata → Text Snippets is where you add your own, and it shows you how quick entry will read the result while you are still typing it.

Snippets expand once and do not nest, and a name Ingest does not recognize is left alone rather than deleted. If two snippets share a name, the first one wins.

Keep exploring your workflow.

Explore Ingest →Find it with ⌘K →

automation.title: Connect the steps in your workflow.
automation.body:
Open verified copies in your editing app, run an action, or connect Ingest to Shortcuts and other tools. Automation is optional; a simple import needs none of it.

Actions Shell scripts The ingest:// scheme Callbacks Your settings as one file

Actions

An action is a named list of steps. Add it in the workspace’s After Import section or in Import Settings. It runs on verified imported copies after metadata processing and receipt persistence succeed. You can also invoke an action from ⌘K on the current selection or from a link.

Each ordered assignment has its own Photos for this action: All imported photos, Tagged, Untagged, or Advanced filters for groups, ratings, keywords, labels, file types, and destination rules. Different categories must all match; any selected value within a category can match. Preview shows the matching count. This is separate from Photos to import, which chooses what is copied.

For example, import All, open Tagged copies in Lightroom Classic, and reveal Untagged copies in Finder. Empty assignments are skipped with an explanation. Different actions can intentionally share photos. Targets and substitution values are fixed when import starts.

Use a file-based Lightroom action for a subset. A folder-wide Lightroom step cannot honor Tagged or other subset scopes and is rejected for them; it may also include files already in the destination folder. Successful actions are recorded and do not run again when retrying unfinished work. A failed required action prevents automatic card cleanup.

Ingest ships with three: open the copies in Lightroom Classic, reveal them in Finder, and import them into an Apple Photos album. Edit them or delete them.

StepWhat it does
Open in an appHands the copied files to an app you choose, the same as dragging them onto it.
Import into an Apple Photos albumOpens a reviewed Send to Apple Photos sheet after ingest and backups finish. Existing JPEGs or JPEG companions are selected by default; RAW choices are explicit. Choose or create the destination album before sending. The name can use {yyyy}, {mm}, {dd}, {address}, and {city}, so {yyyy}-{mm} Ingest files each month separately. Photos reads metadata present in the imported files. Confirmed Ingest imports can be reused using content receipts. This action is unavailable when Apple Photos integration is disabled in Settings.
Copy to a folderA second copy somewhere else, after the first one is verified.
Reveal in FinderOpens the destination with the new files selected.
Add the Finder tag “Ingested”So Finder, Spotlight, and rules in other apps can see which files came through.
Run a ShortcutRuns a shortcut from the Shortcuts app by name, with the file paths as its input. The picker lists the shortcuts you have.
Run a shell scriptRuns zsh. Described below.

Turn on Ask before running for anything you want to see coming. Every run is logged, and the log is shown in Settings next to the action so you can tell what happened without hunting for a file.

Shell scripts

A script step runs zsh. The file paths arrive on standard input, one per line, and four variables are set:

VariableValue
$INGEST_FILESThe path of a file that lists every copied path.
$INGEST_DESTINATIONWhere they were copied to.
$INGEST_ADDRESSThe job address, if one was set.
$INGEST_COUNTHow many files.

The step starts with a line that does nothing but report, which is a good habit to keep while you are working out what you want:

echo "$INGEST_COUNT files in $INGEST_DESTINATION"

A script runs as you. It has your permissions and Ingest does not restrain it. Only add scripts you wrote or understand, and turn on Ask before running while you are still testing one.

The ingest:// scheme

Ingest answers links. Anything that can open a URL can drive it: a Shortcut, a script, a Stream Deck button, a Raycast command, a note on your desktop.

The easiest way to find the link for something is to open ⌘K, highlight the row, and choose Actions → Copy Link or press ⇧⌘C. The palette confirms the copy and stays open. The link is on your clipboard. Values have to be percent encoded the way any URL does, so a space becomes %20.

Links use the same commands, eligibility checks, and confirmation settings as the app. They do not bypass memory-card protection or the review required for a file operation.

LinkWhat it does
ingest://open?path=…Opens that folder.
ingest://cardOpens the mounted card. Add name= to pick one when several are in.
ingest://ingestOpens Import Settings for the current card or folder with the supplied settings. Review the scope and destinations, then click Import to start copying. Takes favorite, destination, template, subfolder, and preset. Giving a template turns renaming on.
ingest://select?paths=…Selects those files in the open source. Comma separated.
ingest://apply?text=…Runs a quick entry line against the selection, snippets and all.
ingest://workspace?name=…Switches workspace.
ingest://split?name=…Shows a split.
ingest://action?name=…Runs an action on what is selected.
ingest://command?id=…Runs any command by its id, available through the Command Palette’s Actions → Copy Link for commands that have no link of their own.

When a link cannot be carried out, the status bar says why in plain words: no folder at that path, no card is mounted, no workspace with that name, that command is unavailable right now.

Callbacks

Every link takes x-success and x-error, in the x-callback-url style. Ingest opens your success URL with a paths parameter listing what it acted on, or your error URL with an errorMessage. That is what lets a Shortcut hand work to Ingest and carry on when it comes back.

Callback URLs are values inside a URL, so they need encoding twice over. Build them with a tool rather than by hand.

Your settings as one file

Settings, Advanced exports everything you have set up as a single .ingestsettings file: options, name templates, metadata presets, snippets, splits, workspaces, actions, and your keyboard shortcuts. That is the file to keep as a backup and to carry to another Mac.

Importing offers two choices. Merge adds what you do not already have and leaves your own items alone. Replace makes this Mac match the file. Either way ⌘Z puts it back, because the import is recorded as one undoable step.

The file holds no photographs, but it can carry destination paths, addresses you have used, your keyword history, and the text of any scripts in your actions. Share it deliberately.

Restore Defaults is next to it, and puts every page back to how Ingest shipped while keeping your favorites, your sequence number, and the marks on your photographs.

Keep exploring your workflow.

Explore Ingest →Find it with ⌘K →
